questions.title: Which club will Rodri join from Manchester City during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Rodri is a midfielder for Manchester City.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from the clubs involved, corroborated by reliable sports reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the receiving club in Rodri's first completed permanent transfer from Manchester City during the 2026 summer transfer window. Transfer rumours, bids, and agreements in principle do not qualify. Resolution Date : The date the completed transfer is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The receiving club's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-24/26 Tier-1 shift (The Athletic via Hindustan Times/OneFootball/The Hard Tackle, TalkSport's Ben Jacobs & Mundo Deportivo/Sergio Valentín via Yahoo Sports): overturning earlier denials, The Athletic reports Real Madrid have moved Rodri to the centre of their summer transfer plans (prepared to offer a contract to 2030), are increasingly confident of reaching an agreement, and are 'operating on the basis that Rodri will be joining the club this summer.' Ben Jacobs adds Manchester City are bracing for a Madrid offer as Rodri wants to leave for football and family reasons, and Mundo Deportivo reports Rodri has given the green light to Madrid while his camp expects City to ask around €80m (versus €50m-€60m cited by AS/Jacobs with one year left on his deal). Zero competing club bids have emerged (Atletico just signed Lee Kang-in; Barcelona signed Anthony Gordon). Lifting Real Madrid from 0.48 -> 0.55 (capped at 0.55 since formal club-to-club talks have not yet begun, City still hope to keep him, and pending back surgery adds execution risk), trimming Atletico Madrid (0.15 -> 0.14), Barcelona (0.13 -> 0.11), PSG (0.10 -> 0.08), and Bayern Munich (0.04 -> 0.03), with 9% residual.

questions.title: If Bradley Barcola leaves Paris Saint-Germain on a permanent transfer during the 2026 summer transfer window, which club will sign him?
questions.background: Bradley Barcola is a French winger playing for Paris Saint-Germain.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Paris Saint-Germain or the receiving club confirming Bradley Barcola’s completed permanent transfer during the 2026 summer transfer window, corroborated by reliable contemporary news reporting. Resolution : Resolve when the transfer is officially confirmed. If more than one permanent transfer occurs during the window, use his first destination after leaving Paris Saint-Germain. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the destination football club.
questions.current_reasoning: Fabrizio Romano reported on June 23 that PSG contract talks with Bradley Barcola (two years left) have stalled after he was benched in the Champions League semi-finals and final, placing Arsenal and Liverpool at the front of the queue. Multiple June 13-18 reports (The Independent, FootballTransfers, Goal) indicate Arsenal lead the race and are preparing a formal bid as Andrea Berta and Mikel Arteta prioritize upgrading left wing, while Le10Sport/TEAMtalk report Barcola is thrilled by Andoni Iraola's Liverpool (though Liverpool's active €100m bid priority is RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande). Bayern Munich (after missing Anthony Gordon), Manchester United, and Barcelona (reported €50m bid rejected June 13, constrained after Gordon) cover secondary elite destinations (~13% field).

questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the clubs involved or reliable contemporaneous news reporting confirming Solomon's completed transfer from Tottenham Hotspur during the summer 2026 transfer window. Resolution : Resolve when the receiving club confirms the signing or the completed transfer is reliably reported. Transfer rumours and ongoing negotiations do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club signing Solomon.
questions.current_reasoning: On June 24, Football London reported Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi told Manor Solomon he is surplus to requirements and available for a cut-price permanent transfer. Former loan clubs Leeds United (where he posted 10G/13A in 2024-25 promotion, though they signed Noah Okafor last summer) and Fiorentina (where he finished 2025-26 on loan with a €10m option and his agent insisted a return remains open) lead early links, alongside Crystal Palace (who submitted a deadline-day deal sheet for him in 2025), Fulham, and West Ham. Because De Zerbi's decision only broke today and no bids have materialized, nearly half the probability mass (~48%) remains on the wider Premier League, Serie A, and European field.

questions.title: Which city will be the site of Typhoon Dolphin's first landfall in mainland China in August 2026?
questions.background: Dolphin developed into a typhoon over the Pacific in late July 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Landfall information issued by China's meteorological authorities, either directly or through contemporaneous reliable news coverage. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the city identified as the location of Dolphin's first mainland China landfall during August 2026. Offshore island landfalls do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the city name, rather than its province or a broader geographical region.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Typhoon Noul's July 26 landfall in Huizhou, Guangdong, Tropical Storm Dolphin (13th named storm of 2026) formed today, July 27 at 17:00 local time, over the far eastern Western Pacific near 13.3N, 176.4E (Dimsum Daily/CMA/JMA/KMA/HKO). Agency guidance forecasts rapid intensification to super typhoon strength by July 30-August 1 and a general northwestward track toward Japan's main islands (Honshu/Kyushu) and possibly Korea around August 5-6. Conditioning on Dolphin taking the western edge of the ensemble spread to make a mainland China landfall (~August 6-8, excluding offshore islands like Zhoushan), South China (Zhanjiang, Guangdong) is virtually eliminated and landfall mass shifts sharply northward to the East China Sea and Yellow Sea coastline: Ningbo (0.10), Shanghai (0.10), Taizhou (0.09), Wenzhou (0.07), and Yancheng (0.07), leaving 57% across other mainland coastal cities (Nantong, Qingdao, Weihai, Dalian, Lianyungang, Rizhao, Ningde, Fuzhou, Jiaxing).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Updating our August 1-13 full-nuclear-fleet drought shutdown forecast on the same July 1-7 European nuclear evidence plus June 26 Swiss shutdown details. Romania surges into #2 (0.13 -> 0.26): Cernavoda Unit 1 was offline in a planned outage on July 1 leaving Unit 2 as the sole operating reactor, early August is peak lower-Danube drought season (matching Cernavoda's August 2003 complete low-water shutdown), and the resolution rule explicitly highlights 'initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor.' Slovenia trims from an inflated prior (0.36 -> 0.28) after NEK confirmed July 6 that Krsko maintained 100% reactor power through June's record heatwave via cooling towers, though a single-reactor Sava plant remains #1 in severe drought. Switzerland trims (0.24 -> 0.19): while Axpo did shut down both Beznau reactors June 26 when the Aare hit 25C (proving strong regulatory readiness to shut down), Switzerland's other two plants (Gosgen and Leibstadt) use evaporative cooling towers and remained online through the June heatwave, making a simultaneous complete national fleet drought shutdown harder than in 1-2 reactor countries unless scheduled August refueling coincides with extreme Aare low flow. Hungary trims (0.16 -> 0.14) given Paks's July 7 output restoration and ministerial exemption override; Bulgaria rises (0.07 -> 0.10) on lower-Danube risk to Kozloduy's 2 units (Slovakia confirmed June 24 its cooling-tower plants have ample water; sum 0.97).
